exercises: an operation with no responses key, and an operation with an empty responses object
note: Deliberately invalid. `responses` is required on an operation in OAS 3.0, and the responses object must carry at least one code, so both forms are rejected. They are both common in a hand-written or half-generated document, which is when a browser gets pointed at one.
doNotChangeFixture: Assertions marked pending describe correct behaviour the browser does not have yet. A failure on one of them is a backlog item, not a fixture defect. Do not edit this fixture or its expectations to match what the app currently does.

expected.assert: Both operations render, listed under their paths, with their summaries.
Neither form throws. An absent key and an empty object are handled the same way.
Neither shows a blank or partial responses section, or a heading with nothing under it.
Both say, in words, that the document describes no responses for this operation.
expected.why: The responses section is omitted entirely when there are none, so the reader cannot tell an undocumented operation from a rendering that failed.
